data.why: The repo bundles three full Italian novels by Svevo under examples/ specifically as sample corpora for the upload workflow, so these are handed to the browser as upload test files instead of writing synthetic text.

goals: Discover latent thematic clusters (topics) in a literary corpus without manual close reading of every page
Tune preprocessing (language, POS filter, custom stopwords, chunk size) to get interpretable, non-noisy topics
Evaluate model quality via C_v coherence score and a coherence sweep to pick a defensible number of topics
Trace exactly which tokens were kept, lemmatized, or removed at each preprocessing step for methodological transparency
See how topics are distributed across documents/chunks (heatmap, distribution, diachronic view) to connect topics back to text structure
Export reproducible results (CSV, PDF report, ZIP with environment info) for citation in scholarly work

review.summary: The tree captures what Lemmata is for, judging and interpreting LDA topics in literary texts, and most of the cited screens match their nodes closely. The setup stage, though, leaves out the language, POS and parameter choices the README treats as the core workflow, and the stopword, excerpt and export claims need correcting before filing.
